title: GTA 6 Pre-Orders Are Coming In 'Far In Excess' Of What Take-Two Expected, Says CEO
text: GTA 6 Pre-Orders Are Coming In 'Far In Excess' Of What Take-Two Expected, Says CEO Skip to content Kotaku Latest Entertainment Reviews News Tips & Guides Games Downloads Deals Games GTA 6 Pre-Orders Are Coming In ‘Far In Excess’ Of What Take-Two Expected, Says CEO 'Tracking far above our initial expectations' By Rebekah Valentine Published November 9, 2026 | Comments ( 0 ) | 𝕏 Copied! © Rockstar Games There’s just over a week left before Grand Theft Auto 6 ‘s launch, and by all accounts it sounds like it’s going to be massive. It feels like GTA 6 is everywhere, and early reports have suggested that the $100 digital deluxe edition is outselling even the $80 regular version. Even the CEO of Rockstar owner Take-Two is saying he’s surprised by how well the game is selling already, claiming in the company’s quarterly earnings that its pre-orders are “tracking far above our initial expectations.” Pre-order incentives have been plentiful in recent weeks, with Walmart offering a “ surprise ” of some sort, and a lot of free bonus content bundled in no matter where you buy it . Digital pre-loads begin tomorrow , but physical pre-orders are a code in a box, so you won’t be able to redeem it until the day of. Physical discs won’t be available at launch . What’s more bonkers to me than a nebulous “exceeded expectations” on pre-orders is that GTA 5 is still selling roughly five million copies per quarter, reaching nearly 235 million copies sold in the last few months. I’ve been watching Take-Two’s earnings for years now, and I don’t think I can remember a time when GTA 5 wasn’t selling at least five million per quarter. But if there were a time for it to drop off, I’d say now would be it, given that a brand new game is coming out imminently. And yet! The franchise overall has sold nearly 480 million units. Overall, it wasn’t a great quarter for Take-Two, with net bookings down 18 percent year-over-year and net revenue down as well. Take-Two is reiterating its guidance for the year, though, of net bookings of $8 to $8.2 billion: an absolutely bonkers amount of money that can only be explained by a new GTA (net bookings were $6.72 billion last year, and $5.56 billion the year prior). GTA 6 is, curiously, the only upcoming game in Take-Two’s pipeline that has a firm release date at the moment. 2K is preparing its slate of sports titles for next year, and Project ETHOS, BioShock , and Judas are all still in limbo. For now, everything (quite understandably) hangs on GTA 6 . 🕹️ Level up your inbox Don’t miss the latest reviews, news and tips. Sign up for our free newsletter.
